 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:29128
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 7 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 4964 of 2023
 Ku. Neha
 Versus
 Tapeshwar Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Manoj Kumar Soni, learned counsel for the respond

 Misc. Appeal No. 4962 of 2023
 Smt. Meena
 Versus
 Tapeshwar Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Manoj Kumar Soni, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
MISC. APPEAL No. 4968 of 2023  ASHOK AND OTHERS  Versus  TAPESHWAR SINGH AND OTHERS  Appearance:

Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellants.
 Shri Manoj Kumar Soni, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
 ORDER 1.

These appeals have been filed against the common award dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29128 2 MA-4964-2023 10.5.2023 passed in Claim Case Nos.16/2022, 17/2022 and 18/2022 passed by the Addl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Alot, District Ratlam, challenging quantum of compensation.

entities.text: Addl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Alot, District Ratlam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 . M.A.No.4968/2023 has been filed for death of Premlata Rathore, M.A.No.4962/2023 has been filed for injuries sustained by Meena and M.A.No.4964/2023 has been filed for injuries sustained by Neha.
The liability of the Insurance Co. is not under dispute.

Ku. Neha vs Tapeshwar Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50716795/
1

3. Short facts of the case are that on 10.2.2022, deceased Premlata and other two appellants were returning after participating in a marriage function from Ujjain by their car bearing registration No.M.P. 43 CB 1091 to Taal.

The car was being driven by Vijay Rathore, when they reached near Shanti Palace bypass road, respondent No.1 came from the front side driving swift car bearing registration No. M.P. 09 W.J. 6441 in rash and negligent manner he, by coming from wrong side,
dashed into the car of the appellant because of which all of them sustained grievous injuries.

Deceased Premlata Rathore was rushed to a hospital at Ujjain from where she was brought to a higher center ie., Medi Care Hospital and Research Center, Indore where she was kept on ventilator support.

entities.text: Medi Care Hospital and Research Center, Indore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
However, she succumbed to injuries on 14.2.2022.
4.

The appellants / claimants filed their separate claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation for the death of Premlata and for injuries sustained by Neha and Meena.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence brought on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,57,698/- for death of Premlata

out of which an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29128 3 MA-4964-2023 amount of Rs.7,00,000/- was for loss of dependency.
For injuries sustained by Neha an amount of Rs.1,96,698/- was awarded and in the case of Meena a total amount of Rs.1,29,077/- was awarded.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that as far as the case of deceased Premlata is concerned, the income of the deceased has not been assessed properly.

He submits that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from the business of selling Papaddum, pickle etc.
However, the claims tribunal has disbelieved the said claim and on notional basis income was considered at Rs.5000/- per month.

He submits that this could not have been done by the claims tribunal considering the fact that even if the entire claim of the income of the deceased is to be disbelieved still she has to be considered as an house maker as she was married and raising two children.

As such her contribution to the family cannot be taken any less than the earning members of the family and as such her income atleast should have been taken as per the minimum wages prevalent at the relevant time for an unskilled labour.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation.
6 . As regards the injuries sustained by Neha the learned counsel for the appellant points out that Neha suffered several injuries including injury on her left cheek, on her head.
She also suffered fracture of her left upper limb for which she was operated upon and a plate was inserted.
She was taking tuition and earning through the same.
However after the accident she is not able to continue taking tuition classes.
As regards the injuries for Meena he submits that she sustained fracture on the head because of which there was clotting.
She suffered 35 stitches on her face and also broken teeth.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29128 4 MA-4964-2023
She also suffered fracture on her right wrist.
She remained hospitalized for 4 days.
He submits that in view of these injuries compensation should have been awarded for pain and suffering suffered by her separately which has not been done by the claims tribunal.
Apart from this he points out that Meena suffered permanent disability.
Neha suffered over all 14 % permanent disability in her upper left limb, which has been reduced by the claims tribunal to 8% without any reason or rhyme.

He also submits that Meena Ku. Neha vs Tapeshwar Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50716795/
2 suffered 10% permanent disability with respect to over all body as per the doctor.

entities.text: Meena Ku. Neha vs Tapeshwar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the same has been reduced by the claims tribunal to the extent of 5% without any reason or rhyme.
He thus prays for enhancement of the compensation in all these heads.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co. submits that the claimants in the case of deceased Premlata were not able to prove her business and earning of Rs.20000/- per month therefrom.
The claims tribunal has clearly recorded the findings in para 35 with respect to the same hence the assessment of income on notional basis at Rs.5000/- per month is correct.

As regards the injuries and permanent disability suffered by the other two persons namely Neha and Meena he refers to findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 26 of the impugned award and submits that Dr. O.P. Gupta (A.W.4) who has proved the permanent disability and injuries and has issued permanent disability certificate was not the treating doctor.
He thus submits that the tribunal has correctly assessed the permanent disability independently.
He further points out that even the doctor (A.W.4) in his cross examination has admitted that there is no malunion of the bones.
It has also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29128 5 MA-4964-2023 been accepted by him that there may be reduction of 1% to 2% in the accident of permanent disability.
He has given the certificate as a private doctor.

The appellant have not brought permanent disability certificate from the institutions where they were treated although those institutions were reputed institutions which itself shows that the appellants have not suffered permanent disability to the extent asserted by them.

8. In reply to the arguments of the learned counsel for the Insurance Co., learned counsel for the claimants / appellants places reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Abid Khan V/s. Dinesh & Ors. reported as 2024 ACJ 2142 and submits that once the certificate has been given with respect to over all body, the tribunal could not have reduced the same on its whims.

entities.text: Abid Khan V/s. Dinesh & Ors. reported as 2024 ACJ 2142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties perused the record.
10.

The determination with respect to MA.No.4968/2023-deceased Premlata, it is seen from the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 35 of the impugned award as well as on perusal of the statement of Sumeet Rathore (A.W.1) that apart from a mere assertion of income at Rs.20000/-
per month by selling food items like Papaddum, pickel etc there is no material worth mentioning to even slightly indicate that the deceased was doing such work.
As such in the considered view of this Court the claims tribunal has correctly disbelieved the said claim.
However as it has repeatedly been held and stated by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the contribution of a house maker is no lesser than the contribution of an earning member of the family.

As such, in the considered view of this Court the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29128 6 MA-4964-2023 income of the deceased Premlata should have been taken at least in accordance with the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled labourer at the relevant time.

On perusal of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, it is seen that the minimum wages for an unskilled labour at the relevant time were Rs.8,800/- per month which is taken as the income of the deceased.

Rest of parameters as contemplated by the claims tribunal are correctly applied hence after change in the income of the deceased the compensation for loss of dependency would now come to Rs.12,32,000/- and the total compensation would come to Rs.15,89,693/- after deducting the amount already awarded by the Ku. Neha vs Tapeshwar Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50716795/

3 claims tribunal at Rs.10,57,693/-, the enhanced amount would come to Rs.5,32,000/- which shall be paid to the appellant in M.A.No.4968/2023 over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal with an annual interest at the rate of 6% from the date of filing of the claim petition before the claims tribunal.

11. Determination in M.A.No.4962/2023 and M.A.No.4964/2023-it is seen from the statement of (A.W.4) Dr. O.P. Gupta, as well as from Exhibit P/35 that he has certified the permanent disability of the appellant at 14% with respect to over all body.
However, the same has been considered by the tribunal at 8%.
Exhibit P/35 is the permanent disability certificate issued by Dr. O.P. Gupta.
In the case of Meena, it has been certified as 10%.
However, the tribunal has considered it at 5%.

The reliance has been placed by the learned counsel for the appellant on the judgment of Abid Khan (supra) it is seen that in the said case the permanent disability was issued by the doctor who had treated the claimant in the said case.

However in the present case, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29128 7 MA-4964-2023 no certificate has been issued by the treating doctor.

As regards the proposition put forth by the learned counsel for the appellant that once the doctor has certified the permanent disability with respect to over all body the same cannot be reduced by the tribunal, is not correct.

Even in the judgment relied by the learned counsel the Hon'ble Apex Court in para 6 and 10 has observed as under :-
"6.
Perusal of the award passed by the tribunal as modified by the High Court, would reveal that claimant had sustained compound fracture in the left acetabulum and left rib.
Dr. Alok Mehta (PW-5), who had examined the claimant had deposed that whole body disability suffered by the claimant was to the extent of 17% and this fact has been elicited in the cross-examination.
However, the tribunal computed the compensation towards loss of future income by considering the whole body disability at 10%.
On surmises and conjectures the percentage of disability has been reduced.

No reason whatsoever has been assigned by the tribunal for substituting its opinion to that of the expert opinion namely, the doctor who treated the claimant and examined as PW-5.
10.

In the light of the afore-stated position of law explained when the medical evidence tendered by the claimant is perused, we are of the considered view that tribunal and the High Court committed a serious error in not accepting the said medical evidence and in the absence of any contra evidence available on record,
neither the tribunal nor the High Court could have substituted the disability to 10%
as against the opinion of the doctor (PW-5) certified at 17%.
In that view of the matter the compensation awarded under the head 'loss of income' towards permanent disability deserves to be enhanced by construing the whole body disability at 17%."
12. From the reading of the above quoted para it is clear that the Hon'ble Apex Court has considered that while substituting opinion of the doctor the tribunal has not assigned any reasons.
As such it is absence of reason which was the basis for which the reduction was set aside and not that the opinion of the doctor is binding on claims tribunal.

The proposition of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court is that it is the claims tribunal who has to assess the functional disability with respect to Ku. Neha vs Tapeshwar Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50716795/
4 permanent disability sustained by a person.

entities.text: Ku. Neha vs Tapeshwar Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However that must be based on reasons.
In the present case the claims tribunal in para 26 has given its reasons for reducing the extent of permanent disability.

The tribunal has considered the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29128 8 MA-4964-2023 doctor who had issued permanent disability certificate has admitted that the fracture of bones have properly joined and there is no malunion.
It has also been recorded by the claims tribunal that he has admitted that there may be chances of reduction by 1% to 2% in the extent of permanent disability.
It has also been considered by the tribunal that the doctor who has issued certificate was not the treating doctor.
Thus in the opinion of the tribunal this can be a consideration while assessing the extent of permanent disability with respect to functional disability of the claimants.

Considering the cross examination of the Dr. O.P. Gupta this Court is of the considered opinion that though the reduction in the extent of permanent disability is based on reasons but the extent of reduction is not proper.
In the case of Neha the over all disability has been reduced from 14% to 8% and in Meena's case, it has been reduced from 10% to 5%.

As the doctor himself has suggested that there may be reduction of 1% to 2% which could have been taken by the claims tribunal upt to the extent of 5% looking to the parts where the injury was sustained by the appellant.

Considering that both the persons have suffered several injuries and remained hospitalized for some period and under treatment for a considerable time, this Court is not inclined to reassess the compensation in different heads instead it is considered proper to award a lump sum amount in both the cases respectively.

Thus in the case of Neha in the considered view of this Court a further amount of Rs.2,50,000/- is awarded over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal which would constitute a just and proper compensation and in the case of Meena an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- over and above the amount already NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29128 9 MA-4964-2023 awarded by the claims tribunal.
This amount (in both the cases) shall carry the interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the claims tribunal.

13. In M.A.No.4968/2023 the appeal has been valued at Rs.5.00 lakhs whereas the amount is Rs.5,25,000/- therefore, the appellant is directed to pay deficit Court fees within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
In case of failure to pay deficit Court fees within the period of four weeks, the appellants will not be entitled for interest beyond the period of four weeks.
14. With the aforesaid, the appeals stand disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
